AS-GLOBAL-001.norm: Every world, character, creature, item and effect cell is a multiple of the 48 px grid. 1 cell = 5 ft.

AS-GLOBAL-002.norm: DEC-011: every layer renders at 1 source pixel = 1 screen pixel. No blur, bloom, glow shader, ColorMatrix, parallax, or alpha fade.

AS-GLOBAL-003.norm: Alpha is binary: 0 or 255. Brightness comes from drawn frames and palette ramps.

AS-GLOBAL-004.norm: Ramp ids are the colour vocabulary. uf.hex is the runtime canonical palette now (ADR-002). deus_master_world_palette_v1.hex is the approved target. Assets name ramps. They do not invent hex.

AS-GLOBAL-005.norm: One light direction: top-left, 315 degree azimuth, 45 degree elevation, baked into the frames. Highlights on top and left. Shadows on bottom and right.

AS-GLOBAL-006.norm: Selout is a 1 px outline on the outer silhouette only, using the darkest step of the local ramp, darker on the bottom and right. No universal black. Ground fills have no outline.

AS-GLOBAL-007.norm: Contact shadow is a drawn ellipse at the shadow anchor. Seamless ground tiles carry no baked cast shadow. No drop-shadow filter.

AS-GLOBAL-008.norm: Draw order back to front: ground, strata faces and ramps, objects, unit body, equipment, effects, UI.

AS-GLOBAL-009.norm: Equipment draws in DEUS_Anim slot order: feet, legs, waist, armor, torso, neck, shoulders, arms, hands, ring1, ring2, head, eyes, back, offHand, shield, mainHand, weapon.

AS-GLOBAL-010.norm: Catalogue id is BAND_BIOME_CATEGORY_TYPE_VARIANT_STATE: six fields, letters and digits, hyphen inside a field.

AS-GLOBAL-011.norm: A leading $ is one character on the sheet. A leading ! is an object with no foot offset. Eight characters per sheet when the $ is absent: 4 by 2 blocks.

AS-GLOBAL-012.norm: A character or layer sheet has a sidecar of the same basename with frameWidth, frameHeight, anchor, footprint, facings, animations, frameMs.

AS-GLOBAL-013.norm: An RMMZ charset block is 3 columns by 4 rows. Walk playback is stand, left, stand, right. The walk block is never given a fifth facing row.

AS-GLOBAL-014.norm: A face sheet is 576 by 288, eight 144 by 144 cells, 4 columns by 2 rows.

AS-GLOBAL-015.norm: SV battlers (9 by 6 motions of 64 by 64, sheet 576 by 384) are required for humanoids and for creatures Medium or larger. Tiny and Small critters have none. SV does not replace map rows.

AS-GLOBAL-016.norm: Large frames are 48 by 96 (tall) and 96 by 48 (long). Extra action rows are further $ sheets or sidecar rows. They do not break the 3 by 4 walk read.

AS-GLOBAL-017.norm: Runtime scale, rotation, flip-as-a-substitute, and tint are not a substitute for a drawn frame. Weapon angles are chosen from pre-drawn cels.

AS-GLOBAL-018.norm: DEC-013 geometry: 32 layers, 1 cell = 5 ft, 1 layer = 10 ft, 5 strata of 2 ft, nine races. Home-layer assignment stays open.

AS-GLOBAL-019.norm: DEC-030 bands and biomes are the vocabulary. Legacy catalogue band and biome tokens are not yet mapped and are unknown, not a pass.

AS-GLOBAL-020.norm: SRD 5.1 is the rules authority. V64 is retired. Presentation follows SRD conditions, damage types, sizes and spells.

AS-GLOBAL-021.norm: DEC-016: the scale chart governs drawn size. Numeric source game/data/DEUS_ScaleRegistry.json. Picture art/reference/DEUS_HUMAN_SCALE_STRIP_V1.png. Catalogue copy art/catalogue/scale_chart.json.

AS-GLOBAL-022.norm: Characters and creatures use four directions, row order South, West, East, North.

AS-GLOBAL-023.norm: A sheet that declares SW, NW, NE or SE is a legacy 8-way source. Mine S, W, E, N only. The diagonals are not standard.

AS-CRIT-001.norm: Tiny and Small creatures require idle, walk, attack, hurt and death, each in four directions.

AS-CRIT-002.norm: Fly and swim rows are optional. When declared they use the same four directions.

AS-CRIT-003.norm: A critter has a corpse sprite and a harvest icon. It has no face.

AS-CRIT-004.norm: Frame size follows the frame class. Tiny, Small and Medium are 48 by 48. Tall Large is 48 by 96. Long Large is 96 by 48.

AS-BEAST-001.norm: Medium and larger creatures include the critter rows plus one attack row per declared natural attack.

AS-BEAST-002.norm: Medium and larger creatures use the same 15 condition treatments as humanoids.

AS-BEAST-003.norm: Medium and larger creatures have an SV battler.

AS-BEAST-004.norm: Large uses the tall or long frame. Huge and Gargantuan frames are integer multiples of 48. The exact multiple is open.

AS-HUM-001.norm: Each of the nine races has a male and a female body template. Today only HUMAN male T0 and HUMAN female T0 exist in the catalogue.

AS-HUM-002.norm: Socket ids are fixed. The human 48 px stand-down baseline is recorded. Other frames store their own coordinates under the same ids.

AS-HUM-003.norm: Part layers: body, eyes, hair front, hair back, beard, and racial ears, horns, tail, scales where that race has them.

AS-HUM-004.norm: Paper-doll z-order is legs 1, torso 2, clothes 2, head 3, back 4, shield 5, held 6, fx 7.

AS-HUM-005.norm: The face shows the same worn armour and helmet as the charset.

AS-HUM-006.norm: Age is a visible axis. Child, adult and a stooped working elder are required. Further steps, including a teen stage, are an open Owner question.

AS-HUM-007.norm: Hair greying is a ramp: natural, salt-and-pepper, grey, white. Balding is a visible locus that masks hair. The mask count is open.

AS-HUM-008.norm: Visible genetic loci and the parts they select are defined here. Inheritance math stays in the sim.

AS-HUM-009.norm: Humanoid action rows cover the charter families and the lane list, four directions each.

AS-HUM-010.norm: Pose families F01 through F14 map onto those rows. F14 frames for sleep, prone, unconscious and dead must be distinguishable. Whether they share one family id is open.

AS-HUM-011.norm: Emotes use the RMMZ balloon sheet: 384 by 720, 8 frames by 15 rows of 48 px.

AS-HUM-012.norm: All 15 SRD conditions have a DEC-011 treatment: pose, frame-freeze, drawn ramp, decal or icon. Invisible is a drawn contour, not a filter.

AS-HUM-013.norm: Pregnancy is a presentation hook with stages 0, 1, 2 and 3: a torso decal per race rig, not a new combat sheet.

AS-HUM-014.norm: dominantHand is right or left. Grips are ONE_HANDED, OFF_HAND, TWO_HANDED, VERSATILE. Asymmetrical gear is not mirrored.

AS-HUM-015.norm: Nine races times 15 outfits (12 classes plus light, medium and heavy armour) is 135 art variants of race-neutral outfit ids.

AS-HUM-016.norm: PM-proposed, Owner may amend: body poses are drawn once. Garb layers match that grid. Weapons and shields pick a pre-drawn angle at a per-frame anchor. No runtime rotation.

AS-HUM-017.norm: Capes, long robes, large shields and bows mid-draw have their own frames for every pose. They are not a single angled cel.

AS-HUM-018.norm: Visible body loci: height and build inside the scale-chart envelope, horns, tail, ears, and a dragonborn scale-colour ramp family.

AS-HUM-019.norm: A child body template and a stooped elder template both carry the work and action rows.

AS-FACE-001.norm: Each race has a faceset background keyed by that race ramp and motif.

AS-FACE-002.norm: Face layers bottom to top: background, optional faction trim, body base, face, hair, worn gear, overlays.

AS-FACE-003.norm: Eight expressions in index order: neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, hurt, determined, afraid.

AS-FACE-004.norm: Face anchors on the 144 px cell: neck base, collar line, chin, eye line, crown.

AS-BIOME-001.norm: Six biomes times five depth bands is 30 sets, plus 15 pairwise transitions and a reserved open-air band.

AS-BIOME-002.norm: Each biome-depth set has ground autotiles, cliffs, ramps (one 10 ft layer over 5 squares), water, vegetation, props, season frames and a ramp id.

AS-BIOME-003.norm: TEMP, WET, ARID and VOLC keep the WG.00.04 physical identities under the DEC-030 ids. COLD and WILD ids are required. Their look is open. HIGH is not a biome.

AS-BIOME-004.norm: Four season states are drawn frame indices. They are not a colour LUT or a ColorMatrix.

AS-BLDG-001.norm: Every faction style uses the same piece ids: foundation, wall, wall top, roof edge, roof fill, door, window, floor, pillar, connector, furniture, workstation, plus ruined and charred states.

AS-BLDG-002.norm: The six style profiles are human_frontier, dwarf_stonehold, elf_glade, halfling_homestead, dragonborn_citadel and goblin_salvage.

AS-BLDG-003.norm: Race, culture and profile gaps are listed and not filled with new lore.

AS-BLDG-004.norm: Function, grammar and style stay separate. The 12 universal building classes are the functional catalog.

AS-ICON-001.norm: One icon grid: 32 by 32 px, 16 columns, row-major index, sheet width 512.

AS-ICON-002.norm: One icon slot for every SRD weapon, armour, shield, material, tool, spell school, condition, status, resource and job.

AS-ICON-003.norm: Rarity and quality are a border or corner mark. They are not a second drawing of the icon.

AS-ICON-004.norm: Icons share the top-left light, the 1 px selout and the palette ramps.

AS-ITEM-001.norm: An item id is race-neutral. One Plate Armor, one item id, one stat block. No Elven Plate Armor.

AS-ITEM-002.norm: Layer art key is itemId + __ + race. Missing race variant falls back to __human, then to nothing. No tint and no other race.

AS-NODE-001.norm: A resource node has full, partly harvested, depleted and regrowing states, a harvest animation, a drop sprite, and one variant per biome.

AS-ANIM-001.norm: Animation is the default. A static asset names an exception on the closed list. The clock is 150 ms.

AS-FX-001.norm: A spell is cast pose, delivery shape, damage-type impact and a sim effect. No per-spell animation.

AS-FX-002.norm: Each delivery shape is one animation with a fixed frame count on the 48 px grid.

AS-FX-003.norm: The 13 SRD damage types each have an impact animation and a ramp id. An unknown type is rejected.

AS-FX-004.norm: Lingering sim effects and concentration, buff, curse and ward auras are data on the spell row.

AS-FX-005.norm: Spell rows validate against UF_SpellVisualTable.schema.json, draft 2020-12. customPiece is a hook and is null in the examples.

AS-FX-006.norm: An effect on another Z layer is drawn in that layer at 1:1, with no blur, tint or scale. Looking down shows it.

AS-FX-007.norm: World effects cover projectile, impact, fire, water and weather, with the frame counts in the animation table.

AS-UI-001.norm: Balloons, selection rings, HP bars, lower-layer overlays and the six faction window skins are drawn frames.

AS-UI-002.norm: Multi-layer selection draws the same ring on each selected unit own layer at 1:1.

AS-UI-003.norm: HP, team and status are readable without colour alone. The smallest UI glyph is 16 px. Icons stay 32 px.

AS-SUMMON-001.norm: Every derived conjure, summon, animate or create-entity spell has a slot in the summon table.

AS-SUMMON-002.norm: Each summon slot has summon-in, dismiss and a controller marker. Creatures also follow the size standard.

AS-REMAIN-001.norm: Remains cover race and creature bodies, skeletons, blood, scorch, rubble, debris, and burned, frozen and flooded tile and building variants.

AS-HAUL-001.norm: Carry is drawn. Carts exist. Stockpiles have fill levels. The old carry-not-drawn rule does not apply.

AS-VEH-001.norm: Carts, wagons, boats and siege engines exist, plus a riding pose per race in four directions.

AS-LIGHT-001.norm: Night is a precomputed ramp plus drawn lights, torch glow, window glow and lit buildings. Optional crisp tint is per-pixel or per-tile, blur stays off, and the hook defaults to off.

AS-MAP-001.norm: World map, minimap, markers and one banner per style profile are specified. No art is produced here.

AS-PROP-001.norm: Shop signs, gravestones, statues and notice boards are readable props and a named static exception.

AS-STYLE-001.norm: File names follow the class patterns. The style-bible sheet is a spec only.

Drawn dither. Binary alpha. Not a blur.

exclude.Gate: Text: "You conjure a portal". A portal is a travel opening, not a creature or a field token.
exclude.Magnificent Mansion: Text: "You conjure an extradimensional dwelling". A place, not a creature or a field token.
exclude.Web: Text: "You conjure a mass of thick, sticky webbing" that fills a cube. Area delivery, not an entity slot.

summonDerivation.method: Include a kind:spell entry when its name starts with Conjure, Animate or Wall of, or its name is in the named list, or its description matches "you conjure" or "you summon", unless the name is in the exclude map. Exclusions are spells whose own text creates a portal, a dwelling or a cube of webbing.

summons.name: Animate Dead
summons.note: Bones become a skeleton. A corpse becomes a zombie. Text of the spell.

summons.name: Animate Objects
summons.note: Spell-defined object. Size is the animated object, Tiny through Huge. Text forbids anything larger than Huge.

summons.name: Arcane Hand
summons.note: Text: a Large hand of force. Spell-defined object, AC 20.

summons.name: Conjure Animals
summons.note: Text: fey spirits that take the form of beasts. The sim picks a beast stat block at cast. No single creature id.

summons.name: Conjure Celestial
summons.note: Text: a celestial of challenge rating 4 or lower.

summons.name: Conjure Elemental
summons.note: Text example: an elemental appropriate to air, earth, fire, or water. CR 5 or lower.

summons.name: Conjure Fey
summons.note: Text: a fey creature of CR 6 or lower, or a fey spirit in the form of a beast of CR 6 or lower.

summons.name: Conjure Minor Elementals
summons.note: Text: elementals in the listed CR options.

summons.name: Conjure Woodland Beings
summons.note: Text: fey creatures in the listed CR options.

summons.name: Create Undead
summons.note: Base text: each corpse becomes a ghoul. Higher slots name ghasts, wights, and mummies.

summons.name: Faithful Hound
summons.note: Text: a phantom watchdog. Invisible to all but the caster. Drawn for the caster with the Invisible contour rule. No sprite for others. Not an alpha filter.

summons.name: Find Familiar
summons.note: Text lists the forms. Frog (toad) uses the frog stat block. Fish (quipper) uses the quipper stat block.

summons.name: Find Steed
summons.note: Text lists warhorse, pony, camel, elk, mastiff.

summons.name: Flaming Sphere
summons.note: Text: a 5-foot-diameter sphere of fire in an unoccupied space.

summons.name: Floating Disk
summons.note: Text: a circular horizontal plane of force, 3 feet in diameter.

summons.name: Forcecage
summons.note: Text: an immobile cube-shaped prison of force, cage or box.

summons.name: Guardian of Faith
summons.note: Text: a Large spectral guardian.

summons.name: Mage Hand
summons.note: Text: a spectral, floating hand. No size word in the text. Frame is one 48 px cell.

summons.name: Phantom Steed
summons.note: Text: a Large quasi-real horselike creature.

summons.name: Planar Ally
summons.note: Text: the entity sends a celestial, an elemental, or a fiend, and the creature appears.

summons.name: Simulacrum
summons.note: Text: a duplicate that is a creature, formed from ice or snow, using the original statistics at half hit points. Sprite is the source creature plus the summon marker.

summons.name: Spirit Guardians
summons.note: Text: spirits flit around the caster to 15 feet. Aura entity on the caster, not a separate stat block.

summons.name: Spiritual Weapon
summons.note: Text: a floating spectral weapon.

summons.name: Unseen Servant
summons.note: Text: an invisible, mindless, shapeless force. Controller sees the Invisible contour. Others see no sprite.

summons.name: Wall of Fire
summons.note: Text: a wall of fire on a solid surface.

summons.name: Wall of Force
summons.note: Text: an invisible wall of force. Drawn as opaque force-ramp panels, not an alpha filter. The SRD word invisible is the rules text. The pixels are the force ramp.

summons.name: Wall of Ice
summons.note: Text: a wall of ice, dome, sphere, or panels.

summons.name: Wall of Stone
summons.note: Text: a nonmagical wall of solid stone.

summons.name: Wall of Thorns
summons.note: Text: a wall of tangled brush.
